A_target.statement:
The [[Definition:Gaussian Integer|Gaussian integers]] $\Z \sqbrk i$ form a [[Definition:Euclidean Domain|Euclidean domain]] with $\map N {a + b i} = a^2 + b^2$.
That is, for $\alpha, \beta \in \Z \sqbrk i$ with $\beta \ne 0$ there exist $\kappa, \rho$ with $\alpha = \kappa \beta + \rho$ and $\map N \rho < \map N \beta$.
Hence $\Z \sqbrk i$ is a [[Definition:Unique Factorization Domain|unique factorization domain]].

B_source.statement:
Let $a, b \in \Z$ with $b \ne 0$.
Then there exist $q, r \in \Z$ with $a = q b + r$ and $\size r \le \dfrac {\size b} 2$, by taking $q$ to be an integer nearest to $\dfrac a b$.

substitutions.the nearest integer: the nearest Gaussian integer, rounding each coordinate

object_map.reformulation: Divide in Q(i) and round each coordinate to the nearest integer, measuring the error with the multiplicative norm.

validity_conditions: The norm is multiplicative, so the remainder norm is N(beta) times the norm of the rounding error.
Rounding each coordinate gives error at most 1/2 in each, so the error norm is at most 1/2; the analogous argument fails for Z[sqrt(-5)].
proof_plan: Write $\dfrac \alpha \beta = x + y i$ with $x, y \in \Q$.
Choose $m, n \in \Z$ with $\size {x - m} \le \dfrac 1 2$ and $\size {y - n} \le \dfrac 1 2$, and let $\kappa = m + n i$.

Let $\rho = \alpha - \kappa \beta = \beta \paren {\dfrac \alpha \beta - \kappa}$.
By multiplicativity of $N$:
:$\map N \rho = \map N \beta \paren {\paren {x - m}^2 + \paren {y - n}^2} \le \dfrac {\map N \beta} 2 < \map N \beta$
